criteria.reasoning: The brief states "Ask: $80,000 — one figure, not a range" and uses $80,000 throughout. No other amount or range is offered.

It identifies the "Largest single household gift in the period: $20,000 on 2025-10-14" from the Vandermolen Family Fund DAF. It excludes the $25,000 Marine Supply sponsorship as "not a household gift, corporate gift" and computes "Cap: 4 × $20,000 = $80,000".

The proposed purpose is "Adult Literacy Program — FY27 program priorities, not part of the campaign", with emphasis on the Upriver pilot and Tutor Corps. The brief says "Do not propose Open Doors" and offers no Open Doors alternative.
The brief says "Do not propose any naming opportunity" and "Offer no public recognition and no naming." It lists Open Doors naming items only to exclude them and suggests no naming of any kind.

The brief says "Treat any gift as anonymous" and "Affirm anonymity: no annual-report listing, no wall, no plaques, no announcements, private letter only". It notes the CRM recognition name but says "the most recent preference for anonymity governs".
It names "Who will be asked: Celeste A. Vandermolen, with Martin J. Vandermolen present" and quotes "Celeste runs our giving — I just sign where she tells me". The ask is directed to Celeste.

The meeting is arranged "only through her personal channels": celeste.vdm@example.net and the home phone (360) 555-0187. The brief explicitly forbids the vandermolenmarine.com emails, the store line and Harbor Way mail. The only setting it proposes is the home, not the company.
It names "Who makes the ask: Teresa Lindahl with leadership partner Lillian Cho" and notes that Celeste requested her and that she has made an FY27 gift. No one else is on the team.
Under "Gregory Hale is recused and takes no part", the brief declines his co-solicitation offer and says not to "involve Gregory Hale or mention the arbitration". He has no role.

The brief never mentions the Rasmussens, Ingrid Rasmussen, a $100,000 endowment gift or a fellow tutor's gift. It gives only a general instruction: "Do not use any other donor's gift as a peer example or benchmark".
The brief sets "Timing: November 2026, after their mid-October financial-advisor meeting", citing "come see us after the advisor meeting". That falls inside the required window.

Every fact about the Vandermolens comes from the files: the gifts, the $382,000 capacity, ages and roles, quotations, contact channels and preferences. No gift, asset, family member or quotation is invented.
